long_biography.plain_text:
Peter Harrison remade Chernikeeff from a marine-instrument maker into Britain's biggest privately owned specialist in business computer networks. He recognised that communications technology offered the stronger future, then directed the shift as chairman and chief executive. After borrowing to acquire the business in 1978, he expanded its enterprise-networking operations and ultimately sold the family interest to Dimension Data.

That achievement followed a notably modest start. Born in Cheadle in 1937 to a bus driver and a seamstress, Harrison left school at 16 and qualified as a chartered accountant. He then held executive posts at Ford, Firth Cleveland and Crest Nicholson. The sale financed a £30 million foundation endowment, later supplemented with further capital for adaptive sport, special-needs provision and education for young people facing disadvantage. His sporting ambition also drove Britain's return to the America's Cup after a 14-year absence. Harrison was appointed CBE for charitable services, received an Antiguan knighthood for philanthropy and died at his Reigate home aged 84.
